findings.issue: 何 before the particle が is read なに, never なん (なん occurs only before だ/で/と/の and counters). The kana transcribes 何が as なんが, teaching a wrong pronunciation.
findings.current: そのほんにわなんがかいてあるの?
findings.suggested: そのほんにわなにがかいてあるの?

findings.issue: Token 何 has reading なん, but before が the standard reading is なに (なにが). Wrong reading in context.
Romaji propagates the wrong reading of 何が as 'nan ga'; should be 'nani ga' (same fix as kana).
この is called 'conectivo' (connective), which is a wrong word-class label; この is a demonstrative (pré-nominal/連体詞). expl_en correctly says 'demonstrative', so the two versions are inconsistent.
findings.current: O conectivo この ('este') aponta para um objeto próximo do falante.
findings.suggested: O demonstrativo この ('este') aponta para um objeto próximo do falante.

findings.issue: こんな is proximal ('this kind of / such'); 'that kind of' corresponds to そんな/あんな and muddles the ko-so-a series for learners. The pt gloss and lit_en ('this early') use the proximal sense.
お前に is the causee marked by dative に, not a topic; rendering it 'As for you' misuses the course's は-mirror device. lit_pt correctly mirrors it as 'A você'.
findings.current: As for you, I can't let you do such a thing.
findings.suggested: To you, such a thing — I can't let (you) do it.

findings.issue: 'Intended to have visited' is dated/awkward English (perfect infinitive); natural modern rendering of 〜つもりだった is 'intended to visit'. Meaning unchanged.
findings.current: He intended to have visited the temple last week.
findings.suggested: He intended to visit the temple last week.
